svg.text: ONE-PIECE FOLD-OVER TEMPLATE — print, cut, fold, punch:
1. Print at 100% / "actual size" (not "fit to page") — likely needs A3 or a tiled/large-format print; measure
the 50mm calibration bar below with a ruler before trusting it.
2. Cut around the OUTER outline of the combined shape (back-wall panel + lid panel together).
3. Fold 90° along the thick dashed FOLD LINE, so the back-wall panel folds down and away from the lid panel
(same direction as opening a hinged lid) — ink stays facing outward on both panels after folding.
4. Drape it over the actual enclosure: lid panel flat on top, folded back-wall panel hanging down the real
back wall. Dry-fit and check alignment before marking anything.
5. Center-punch through the paper at every solid black dot, on both panels.
back-wall panel (floor edge at top, fold/hinge edge at bottom)
USB coupler bore ⌀23.7
flange 26x31 (ref only,
not a cut line)
— FOLD 90° HERE (box's back-top edge) —
RESET ⌀12
TUNER/MUTE ⌀12
ENCODER ⌀7.1
OLED cutout ~58x30
(center ref only — cut, not drilled)
PRESET ⌀12
SNAPSHOT ⌀12
(Y=52, same as OLED center)
50mm — measure this line after printing to confirm scale
All hole positions are center-to-center from the box's back-left corner — see pipedal-hardware-v2.md
§2.1 (lid) and §2.3a (back wall) for the same coordinates as tables. Cut this template to match your
ACTUAL enclosure size before marking anything — nominal box dimensions, not a measurement of yours.
Solid black dots mark the exact center of every drilled hole — center-punch through those, not by
eyeing the circle. Dashed squares (13.4x12.1mm) on every footswitch show the ACTUAL base, confirmed
from the A-1874 datasheet — bigger than the ⌀12mm hole, on the front/outside face. Not keyed to the
round hole, so rotate each switch to whichever angle clears its neighbours best.
USB coupler positioned off-center (X=170, not centered at X=111) on purpose — centering it there left
only 1.9mm clearance to the OLED module hanging down from the lid; X=170 gives ~10mm/~9mm real
clearance to the OLED and TUNER/MUTE respectively. RESET and TUNER/MUTE moved slightly (to X=22/198)
to clear internal corner posts found inside the physical chassis — see pipedal-hardware-v2.md §2.1.
Still verify all of this once you have the parts — checked against estimated dimensions, not a full dry-fit.

g.text: RESET, TUNER/MUTE, SW1-6, PRESET, SNAPSHOT (10x, ⌀12mm body) — ⌀12mm bit (step-drill #1 bit, 4-32mm)
OLED mounting holes (4x, ⌀3mm, M3) — ⌀3mm bit. Check the OLED module's box first — many ship with their
own M3 screws/standoffs; only buy separate hardware if none came with it.
Preset-browse encoder (1x, ⌀7.1mm) — closest bit in a metric HSS set is ⌀7mm; the encoder's own
nut/washer covers the ~0.1mm slop, no reaming needed.
OLED viewing window (~58x30mm) — not a drill bit: drill a ⌀3-4mm pilot hole inside the waste area,
cut with a rotary tool + cutting disc, then file/sand to the line.
USB coupler bore (1x, ⌀23.7mm, on the back-wall panel) — ⌀24mm bit (step-drill #1 bit, 4-32mm)
USB coupler mounting screws (2x, ⌀3.4mm, M3) — ⌀3.5mm bit, or ⌀3mm if that's the closest you have
Corner-post danger zones aren't drawn here (this diagram has none) — see pipedal-hardware-v2.md §2.1
and pipedal-footswitch-drill-template.svg for those. Orient PRESET/SNAPSHOT's narrow (12.1mm) side
toward their LED for max margin (confirmed 7.3mm edge clearance).
same two panels as separate, standalone sheets (the back-wall one is mirrored there for separate use).
